doc.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024

title: Early encouragement and first $3 gig
summary: A first bass teacher said he would always make a living; Beal's first paid job was a $3 kids' dance class.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Right on. Was there a point when you were young that this career sort of came to be a possibility to you? Did you have what we would now call an epiphany or some like moment that just like put you on this path?
I had encouragement from my first bass teacher, who told me that, “You’ll always make a living playing the bass.” So that gives you confidence you know, when you hear something like that.

Because that’s what I played and that’s my focus you know? And I’m talking junior high school or high school. I guess it was high school you know, and then you know you get hooked as soon as you make a couple of bucks playing something you like you know. I played for a kids’ dance class on Saturday nights that made $3 and I barely knew the names of the strings. So that was the beginning you know.
That’s one less than I made on my first gig. I made 4.
